text:
sam: Quick question from the all-hands recap: leadership talked about 'unified inference across environments' as a differentiator. For product planning, can we get clarity on what we will *not* do? e.g., will we ever bundle model training or heavyweight model management?

yvonne: Short: we're not a training platform. We will support model variants and onboarding, but not training pipelines or heavyweight data labeling. Our focus stays on serving, observability, and migrations.

oscar: For roadmapping: does the 'unified' promise mandate parity of features across Hosted/Dedicated/Private immediately? Or is it ok to have a staggered rollout?

maria: Staggered rollout is fine. Prioritize parity for core SLOs and APIs; enterprise-only extras (e.g., HSM KMS integrations) can be gated.

trent: From strategy: competitor watchers will attempt to paint us as "just an infra layer." How should we respond?

strategy-bot: Playbook draft: "We are a developer platform that optimizes the economics and reliability of inference. We ship a curated model catalog, but our product promises are about serving outcomes, not owning models."

sam: Thanks. One final thing 10% of customers ask about self-hosted open-source runtimes vs using Redwood Private. Any guidance for field teams on the business case?

yvonne: Guidance: Redwood Private is for teams wanting product-grade ops, auditability, and support. If they want to run OSS to save cost and have internal infra expertise, that's fine but we should offer migration paths and managed services if they scale.

oscar: Great. Can we put these bullets in the Console > Docs as a short "what we are/aren't" page? That would prevent inconsistent messaging.

maria: Agreed. I'll own a short doc and ping the squad for review. ETA EOD Wednesday.
